blocks.text: Cross-entropy loss measures how far a model predicted probability distribution is from the true, correct answer, and it is the loss function underlying nearly every technique covered in this course, from basic classification to the causal language modeling loss that powers most fine-tuning covered in the next topic.
Understanding cross-entropy at a working level makes the remaining topics in this module, each a variation or application of this same core idea, considerably easier to follow.
1. What Cross-Entropy Loss Measures
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785471959036-793949541.png

Cross-entropy loss quantifies the difference between two probability distributions, the distribution the model actually predicted, and the distribution representing the true, correct answer, producing a single number that gets smaller as the model prediction gets closer to correct.
2. From Model Output to a Probability Distribution

blocks.alt: From Model Output to a Probability Distribution
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785471959036-419183553.png

A model does not directly output a clean probability distribution, it produces raw scores, which get converted into an actual probability distribution, values that sum to one, through a function called softmax, covered briefly in earlier topics of this course and central to how cross-entropy loss actually gets computed.
3. Comparing Predicted vs True Distribution
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785471959037-764161991.png

The true distribution in most training setups is a simple one, all probability mass concentrated entirely on the one correct answer, and cross-entropy measures how much probability mass the model prediction placed on that same correct answer, the more it agrees, the lower the loss.
4. Why Cross-Entropy Punishes Confident Wrong Answers

blocks.alt: Why Cross-Entropy Punishes Confident Wrong Answers
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785471959037-701489223.png

Cross-entropy loss grows sharply as the model predicted probability for the correct answer approaches zero, meaning a confidently wrong prediction, one that assigned very low probability to the actual correct answer, gets penalized far more heavily than an uncertain, hedged wrong prediction.

blocks.title: This shapes model behavior in a useful way
blocks.content: Because confident wrong answers are penalized so heavily, training with cross-entropy loss naturally discourages a model from becoming overconfident about incorrect predictions.

blocks.text: 5. The Cross-Entropy Formula, Explained Simply
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785471959037-476292376.png

In the common case where the true answer is a single correct class, cross-entropy loss reduces to a simple calculation, take the probability the model assigned to that correct class, and compute its negative logarithm, a value near zero when the model assigned high probability correctly, growing large as that assigned probability shrinks toward zero.
6. Cross-Entropy as the Default for Classification

blocks.alt: Cross-Entropy as the Default for Classification
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785471959037-942589787.png

Cross-entropy is the standard default loss function for any task that predicts one correct answer from a set of possible categories, whether that is a traditional classification task with a fixed label set, or predicting the next word from an entire vocabulary, exactly the situation covered in the next topic of this module.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Task Type","What the Categories Are"],"rows":[["Traditional classification","A fixed set of labels, such as spam or not spam"],["Language modeling","Every possible next token in the vocabulary"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Cross-Entropy in Language Models

When training a language model, cross-entropy loss is computed treating every possible next token in the vocabulary as a category, and the true answer as whichever token actually came next in the real training text, the exact same underlying calculation as any other classification task, just with an enormous number of possible categories.
8. Reading a Cross-Entropy Loss Value
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785471959037-317073566.png

A cross-entropy loss value close to zero indicates the model is assigning high probability to the correct answers, while a larger value indicates the model predictions are further from correct, the same basic interpretation used throughout the loss curve monitoring covered in the earlier SFT Training Pipeline topic.
9. Cross-Entropy's Relationship to Other Losses in This Module

Every other loss function covered in the remaining topics of this module, causal language modeling loss, sequence-to-sequence loss, and token classification loss, is fundamentally an application or variation of this same cross-entropy idea, applied to a slightly different situation or shape of prediction task.
Worked Example

A model predicting the sentiment of a review as positive, negative, or neutral assigns probabilities of 0.7, 0.2, and 0.1 respectively to those three classes. If the true label is positive, cross-entropy loss computes the negative log of 0.7, a relatively low loss, reflecting that the model assigned reasonably high probability to the correct answer.

If instead the model had assigned only 0.1 probability to positive, the negative log of 0.1 produces a much larger loss value, reflecting that the model was confidently wrong, exactly the kind of prediction cross-entropy is designed to penalize heavily.
Common Mistakes

items: Confusing raw model output scores with an actual probability distribution before softmax has been applied
Assuming cross-entropy loss only applies to traditional classification, missing its central role in language modeling
Misreading a loss value in isolation without comparing it against earlier values in the same training run
Not understanding why a confidently wrong prediction produces a much higher loss than an uncertain wrong prediction

blocks.text: Practice

For a model that assigns 0.4 probability to the correct answer among several classes, calculate the resulting cross-entropy loss by hand, and compare it against the loss if the model had instead assigned 0.9 probability to the correct answer, confirming the relationship between predicted probability and loss.
Key Takeaway

Cross-entropy loss measures how far a model predicted probability distribution is from the true correct answer, growing sharply as the model becomes confidently wrong, and it serves as the foundational loss function underlying classification tasks and language modeling alike, with every other loss covered in this module building on this same core idea.
